# Story 01 — Agent: my own tickets are one click away (Story: CRM-93)

## Prerequisites

- **
TICKETS-2-WEB (the ticket queue) completed** — this story extends `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx` and its hook `web
/src/pages/tickets/useTicketQueue.ts`; both must already exist and keep filters in the URL. Verified present at `web/src/pages/
tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx` and `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketQueue.ts:44` (`KEYS = ['status', 'priority', 'categoryId', 'assig

neeId']`).
- **No API work.** `GET /tickets?assigneeId=<id>` already exists and is what this story uses. Do not tou

ch anything under `api/`.

---

## Story Goal

A signed-in agent can narrow the ticket queue to the tickets assigned to them **in one click**, without typing their own id.

Concretely:

1. The queue page shows a **"My tickets"** action, visible to staff.
2. Clicking it sets `assigneeId=<my id>` in the URL search params and re

-runs the same queue request.
3. The result is **the same queue**: same rows, same paging, same words — just filtered. Not a new route,

not a new screen, not a new hook.
4. The URL carries the filter, so the view is a link a colleague can open and one the back button restores.

This is already how `useSearchParams` treats the other three filters.
5. Every new visible string comes from `en.ts` **and** `ar.ts

` in the same edit (BR-6). Nothing hard-coded in JSX.

Explicitly **not in scope**: any
change under `api/`; any second "my tickets" screen for staff; any change to the customer-facing `/port

al/my-tickets` page.

---

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketQueue.ts` — read the whole file (~97 lines). Note in

particular:
   - Line 15 — `export const UNASSIGNED = 'none'` (the sentinel for "nobody has this one"; the agent's own id is a

real id and needs no sentinel).
   - Lines 44–46 — `KEYS = ['status', 'priority', 'categoryId', 'assigneeId']`; filters are a `Partial<Record<FilterKey, string>>

`.
   - Lines 55–62 — filters come from the URL, one direction.
   - Lines 74–83 — `apply(next)` writes new filters back and resets `offset` to 0.
   -
Line 96 — the hook returns `{ status, error, page, filters, offset, apply, clear, goTo }`. Do **not** add a new hook; call

`apply` with `{ ...filters, assigneeId: me.id }`.
2. `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx` — read the whole file. Note:
   - Around line 60
and line 143 — the assign-dialog use of `UNASSIGN`/`ticket.assigneeId`; **do not confuse** the

*assign a ticket* control with the *filter by assignee* control.
   - Around lines 280–348 — the fil
ter draft state (`draft.assigneeId`, `set('assigneeId', ...)`, `Select`). The new one-click action must feed the **

same** `apply()` call these controls already use so the URL and the request stay in sync.
3. `web/src/shared/session

/use-me.ts` — read the whole file (~49 lines). Uses:
   - Line 29 — `export type Me = { id: string; role: string; name: string }`.
   - Lines 46–

47 — `isAdmin` / `isStaff` return `undefined` while loading. Treat `undefined` as "not yet"; do not render the button in that state.
4. `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` around
**line 215** (`ticketQueue: { … }`) and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` around **line 172** (`ticketQueue: { … }`) — add new le

aves in both files in the same edit. Nested one level deep, camelCase leaves (no dot paths).
5. `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueueP
age.test.tsx` — read especially lines 15–100 (`assigneeId: null` fixture, `lastQuery(calls).get('assigneeId')` assertions at ~l

ines 90 and 96). New tests must follow the same shape (fresh `Response` per call per L-30).
6. `web/src
/testing/stub-me.ts` — read the whole file. Every test that renders anything wrapping the desk shell (or that calls `useMe()`) must stub `/me`

; the queue page does.
7. `web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` and `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — read the top of each to confirm what fails when

a leaf is added to `en.ts` but not `ar.ts`, or when a literal is left in JSX (BR-6).
8. `web/src/pages/tickets/history-
sentence.ts` — read to remind yourself of the bidi-isolate pattern (U+2068 … U+2069, L-51). **Only** relevant if you inter

polate the agent's name into a translated sentence; the simpler design (see below) does not.
9. `scripts/criteria/tickets.

md` around **line 347** — TICKETS-12-WEB acceptance criteria, already inlined in the intake.

Grep to confirm before writing:
- ``grep -n "ticketQueue" web

/src/shared/i18n/en.ts web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts``
- ``grep -n "assigneeId" web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx``
- ``grep -n "useMe" web/src/pages/t

ickets/``

---

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behaviour:** the queue's assignee filter is a `Select`. Setting it to the current ag

ent means picking one's own name out of a list — which is exactly what the criterion refuses.
- **New behaviour:** a
dedicated one-click **"My tickets"** control that sets `assigneeId` to `me.id` without any typing or picking; the same

control (or a companion "Show all") clears that value.
- **Same queue.** No

new route, no new hook, no separate screen for staff — that would put the same rows in two places.

---

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Add the

i18n leaves in both languages (BR-6)

**File:** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` (under the existing `ticketQueue: {

```

**File:** `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` (under the existing `ticketQueue: { … }` block near line 172)

Add the matching Arabic leaves in the **same edit** (or `shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` f
ent any other leaves. Do **not** interpolate the agent's name; the button is a fixed label, so no bidi isolate is needed. If you dec
ide later to add a "Showing tickets assigned to <name>" sentence, that sentence must wrap the name in U+2068 … U+2069 (L-51) — but this story

does not need it.

### 2 — Wire the one-click action into `TicketQueuePage.tsx`

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx`

Changes:

1. Import `useMe` from

`../../shared/session/use-me` and call it at the top of `TicketQueuePage`:
   ```ts
   const { me, isStaff } = useMe();
   ```
2. Locate the filter bar (
the same block that renders the status/priority/categoryId/assigneeId `Select`s around lines 280–348). Add a new button **inside the same filter bar** —

this is one more control on the queue, not a new section:
   - When `isStaff === true` and `me` is present, render a `Button` labelled `t

.ticketQueue.myTickets`.
   - The button's `onClick` calls `apply({ ...filters, assigneeId: me.id })` — reuse the hook's existing `apply`; do not

introduce a second setter.
   - When `filters.assigneeId === me?.id`, render the button in a pressed/active state (`aria-pressed="true"`) and swap its label to `t.ticket
Queue.showAll`; its `onClick` then calls `apply({ ...filters, assigneeId: undefined })` so the assignee filter is removed from the URL. (Removing the key is what `apply` does when

a value is falsy — see `useTicketQueue.ts:77`.)
   - When `isStaff === undefined` (loading) or `false` (customer somehow re

aching this page), do **not** render the button. A customer should not see it, and drawing a control that will later disappear is worse than drawing nothing.
3. Do **not

** change the existing assignee `Select`. It stays as-is so the same URL value round-trips through both controls.
4. Do **not** create any new

file, route, or hook. The route in `web/src/app/routes.tsx` is unchanged.

**Route wiring reminder.** A route
only its author can navigate to is a route that does not exist — but here there is no new route; the "My tickets" button lives on the queue that agents already reach from

the desk shell.

### 3 — No changes required elsewhere

- **No `api/` changes.** Do not edit anything under `api/src

/features/tickets/`.
- **No new route.** Do not touch `web/src/app/routes.tsx`.
- **No new hook.** Do not add a "useMyTickets" for staff — that

already exists for the portal (`web/src/pages/portal/useMyTickets.ts`) and is a different screen for a different role.
- **No change

to the assignee `Select`.** It continues to list assignees; the new button is an additional path to the same URL state.

---

## Ed

ge Cases & Failure Modes

- **`useMe()` still loading.** `isStaff === undefined`. Trigger: first render before `/

me` answers. Expected: button is not rendered (see `use-me.ts:42–47` comment). Enforced where the component gates on `isStaff === true`.
- **Custom
er somehow on the page.** Trigger: a customer types the queue URL. Expected: the button is not drawn; the API refuses the

request regardless (SC-2). Enforced by the same `isStaff === true` gate.
- **Agent already filtered to themselves and clicks the
button again.** Trigger: `filters.assigneeId === me.id`. Expected: the button reads `t.ticketQueue.showAll` and its click removes `assigneeId` from the

URL, leaving other filters intact.
- **Other filters set.** Trigger: agent has `status=open&priority=high` and clicks "My tickets". Expected: `apply({ ...filters, assigne

eId: me.id })` preserves the other three keys and resets `offset` to 0 (see `useTicketQueue.ts:78–80`).
- **Back button after clicking.** Trigger: agent clicks "My tick
ets", then presses back. Expected: URL loses `assigneeId`, `useSearchParams` re-derives filters, request re-runs. This is already how the URL-as

-state design works; no code needed.
- **Link shared with a colleague.** Trigger: colleague opens the URL. Expected: same rows for anyone with permission to see them (
the id is the *agent's* id, not the viewer's). This is the criterion's "sendable link" and

requires nothing extra.
- **`assigneeId === 'none'` (UNASSIGNED) already selected.** Trigger: agent picked "unassigned" in the `Select`, then clicks "My t
ickets". Expected: `assigneeId` overwrites to `me.id`; `'none'` is not preserved. Enforced by `apply({ ...filters, assigneeId: me.id })` shallow-mer

ge order.
- **Missing `me.id`.** Trigger: `useMe()` returned an error. Expected: button is not rendered because `isStaff`

is `undefined` in that state; no click path exists.
- **BR-6 leak.** Trigger: someone types the label directly in JSX. Expected: `web
/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` fails in CI. Do not add fallbacks like `t.ticketQueue.myTickets ?? 'My tickets

'`.

---

## Test Plan

1. **File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.test.tsx` — add a test **"clicking My tickets filters the queue to the

signed-in agent"**:
   - Stub `/me` via `web/src/testing/stub-me.ts` to return `{ id: 'staff-7', role: 'agent', name: 'Sam

' }`.
   - Render the page, wait for the initial `GET /tickets` call.
   - Click the button labelled `en.ticketQueue.myTickets` ("My tickets").
   - Assert the

most recent `GET /tickets` query has `assigneeId=staff-7` (mirror the pattern at line 90: `lastQuery(calls).get('assigneeId')`).
   -

Assert the URL search params (via the test's memory router) contain `assigneeId=staff-7` and **no** `offset` (reset to 0).
2.

Same file — add **"clicking again with the same agent id clears the assignee filter"**:
   - After the first click, the button label switches to `

en.ticketQueue.showAll`.
   - Second click: assert the request query has no `assigneeId` (mirror line 96: `lastQuery(calls).has('assigneeId')).

toBe(false)`).
3. Same file — add **"My tickets is not rendered for a customer"**:
   - Stub `/me` with `role: 'customer'`.
   - Assert `queryByText(en.ticketQueue.myTickets)` is

`null`.
4. Same file — add **"other filters are preserved when My tickets is clicked"**:
   - Preload the URL with `?status=open&priority=high`.
   - Click "My tickets"; assert the new query has all three keys (`status=

open`, `priority=high`, `assigneeId=staff-7`).
5. Every new test uses a **fresh `Response` per call** in the fetch stub (L-30) and stubs `/me` (any component

that reaches the desk shell must — this page does).
6. `web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` — runs automatically; it will fail if `myTickets`/`showA

ll` are added to `en.ts` but not `ar.ts`. Do not modify this test.
7. `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — runs automatically; it will fail if the button label is typ

ed as a literal instead of coming from `t`. Do not modify this test.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend runs:** `cd web && npm test` — the four

new tests pass; `parity.test.ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` remain green.
2. **Frontend builds (typechecks):** `cd web && npm run build` — `tsc -b &&

vite build` succeeds. `npm test` does not typecheck; the build is what proves the types.
3. **Regression — API unt
ouched:** `cd api && npm test` — must remain green. This story ships no `api/` change; running the API suite guards against acc

idental edits.
4. **Regression — no AI attribution:** `grep -rEi "ai|assistant|copilot|claude|gpt" web/src/pages/tickets web/src/shared/i18

n` — must return no new matches introduced by this diff (nothing committed may mention AI assistance).
5. **Manual smoke** (optional, from
`cd web && npm run dev`): sign in as an agent, open the queue, click **My tickets**, confirm the URL gains `?assigneeId=<my id>`, conf
irm the rows show only that agent's tickets, press the browser back button, confirm the filter is removed and the full queue retur
ns. Sign in as a customer and confirm the button is absent from any staff view they should not be se

eing anyway.

---

## Done Criteria

- [ ] A signed-in agent has a **one-click** control on the ticket queue that filters to their own tickets without

typing an id.
- [ ] The result is the **same queue** (same rows, same paging, same words), not a second screen; no new route was added.
- [ ] The filter is carried in the **URL** (

`assigneeId=<agent id>`), so the view is a shareable link and the browser back button restores the previous state.
- [ ] Cl
icking the control a second time (or its "Show all" sibling label) removes the `assigneeId` filter, leaving other filters and pa

ging behaviour intact.
- [ ] The button is not rendered for customers or while `/me` is still loading.
- [ ] Both `en.ts` and `ar.ts` were edited in the same commit (B

R-6); `parity.test.ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` are green.
- [ ] `cd web && npm test` and `cd web && npm run build` both succeed.
- [ ] `cd api && npm test` succeeds and the

`api/` tree has **no** changes in the diff.
- [ ] No commit, doc, or code comment mentions AI assistance.
